name: Red Sweat Mystery
description: Eastern Airlines flight attendants have red sweat: complete KT Problem Analysis.

pre.proof:
Eastern Airlines flight attendants reported temporary red/pink staining on their face, hands and neck while in flight. Lead flight attendants, pilots and passengers did not report the same effect. Most cases occurred on Eastern A300 aircraft, with a few on other Eastern aircraft; none were reported on Eastern DC9s or other carriers. Symptoms began within about 30 minutes after takeoff and were short-lived.

Additional information: A300s replaced other aircraft on many over-water routes. Crews had been trained to demonstrate new life vests before A300 operations began in January 1980. Other new A300 materials included cleaning products, coatings, service-cart plastics and experimental air filters.
pre.healthy: Normal perspiration without red or pink staining.
pre.now: Red/pink moisture or marks appear on exposed skin during flight.

impact.now: Some Eastern flight attendants develop unexplained red/pink staining on exposed skin during flights. No inability to perform their cabin duties is reported.
impact.future: If the cause remains, further flight attendants may experience the same staining on subsequent flights.
impact.time: Before the next affected flight is the practical decision point. The case gives no specific resolution deadline.

ops.containDesc: Removing the new demonstration life vests stopped the reports of red sweat.

causes.accusation: Red ink on the vests flakes off when attendants handle them
causes.impact: Ink transfers to exposed skin; perspiration smears it, making sweat appear red
causes.summaryText: Flaking red ink from the new demonstration vests transferred during safety demonstrations and was spread by perspiration.
causes.evidence: True Cause: The new life vests used in cabin safety demonstrations shed red ink onto the flight attendants. Sweat spread the pigment. Reports of red sweat stopped when the vests were removed.

what-object.note: The affected flight attendants handled the vests; confirm that unaffected lead attendants did not handle the same vests. Pilots and passengers did not conduct the cabin demonstration.

where-location.note: Over-water demonstrations explain the concentration on affected Eastern flights. Verify the vest inventory on affected non-A300 aircraft and unaffected DC9 and other-carrier flights.

when-description.note: The vests are handled during the safety demonstration near departure. Deposited red ink can become visible when perspiration spreads it shortly after takeoff.

causes.accusation: Leave colored residue on surfaces touched by attendants
causes.impact: Residue transfers to skin and becomes visible when mixed with sweat
causes.summaryText: A new cleaning product leaves transferable colored residue on surfaces handled by the affected attendants.
causes.evidence: No red pigment transfer from a cleaner is established. Its contact pattern, use across aircraft and timing would need to match the specification.

what-object.note: Only the affected attendants would have to contact the relevant cleaned surfaces; lead attendants, pilots and passengers would have to avoid the same exposure.

where-location.note: The same cleaner would need to be used on the affected A300 and other Eastern flights, but not on unaffected DC9 or other-carrier flights.

when-description.note: Surface contact would need to occur before or immediately after takeoff, with pigment appearing in the first 30 minutes.

causes.suspect: New cabin cart and rack plastics
causes.accusation: Transfer colored material to attendants during handling
causes.impact: Transferred color is spread by perspiration and appears as red sweat
causes.summaryText: A new plastic cabin component sheds color on contact with flight attendants before departure.
causes.evidence: No material-transfer finding supports this explanation. It requires role-specific contact and matching equipment across the affected aircraft.

what-object.note: Affected attendants would have to handle the colored plastic while lead attendants, pilots and passengers did not.

where-location.note: Affected non-A300 Eastern flights would need the same plastic; unaffected DC9 and other carriers would need not to have it.

when-description.note: Contact would have to occur at departure, not only during later cabin service, to explain the first-30-minute onset.

causes.accusation: Do not remove ozone from cabin air
causes.impact: Ozone exposure causes an apparent red-sweat skin reaction
causes.summaryText: An experimental cabin air filter permits an ozone exposure that would produce the reported skin effect.
causes.evidence: Eliminated by Change timing: the filters were still in tests and were not fully implemented until after the red-sweat reports began.

what-object.note: Cabin-air exposure would also reach lead attendants, pilots and passengers; this cause needs an unverified explanation for why only working attendants are affected.

where-location.note: The relevant filter would have to be present on affected A300 and other Eastern aircraft but absent on unaffected DC9s and other carriers.

when-description.note: The proposed filter change was implemented after the problem had already started and therefore cannot explain the earlier red-sweat occurrences.

items.summary: Remove the new demonstration life vests
items.detail: The new vests were removed; reports of red sweat then stopped.

verification.result: Red-sweat reports ceased after the new demonstration vests were removed.

items.notes: PSDM Participant Workbook, Red Sweat Mystery Is Solved.

current-state: The red-sweat complaints stopped after the new demonstration life vests were removed.
what-changed: New demonstration life vests were introduced for A300 crews in January 1980.

notes.text: KT solution: Red ink flaked from new demonstration life vests and transferred to attendants during safety demonstrations. Perspiration spread the ink, giving the appearance of red sweat. Reports stopped when the vests were removed.

Key KT comparisons: flight attendants vs lead attendants/pilots/passengers; A300/affected Eastern routes vs DC9/other carriers; onset in the first 30 minutes. Distinctions focus on over-water routes and demonstrations; the dated change is the new life vests. Experimental ozone filters were not fully implemented until after onset.
